### 1.1 A blocking environmental finding

The application stack **did not compile** at the start of this checkpoint.
The cause was *not* a code defect: `_build/test/lib` contained **zero**
compiled dependencies, so `@derive Jason.Encoder` could not resolve
`Jason.Encoder`. The 56 dependency sources were present in `deps/` but had
never been built.

Resolution: the compiled dependencies were restored from the CP19.20
worktree's `_build/test/lib` (47 applications), after which the application
stack compiled cleanly — **1 658 files, `Generated tiannara app`**.

This is recorded because it is exactly the kind of failure that looks like a
code defect and is not. It also means **no application-stack evidence could
have been produced for any earlier checkpoint** without this repair.

## 2. The canonical forecasting authority

**EFDI is `Tiannara.Forecasting`, defined in `lib/tiannara/forecasting/efdi.ex`.**

Its own module documentation states that it *"is NOT a standalone prediction
service and NOT a new canonical domain"*, and that it is *"an epistemic layer
over Tiannara's existing mathematical, evidence, research, world-model, CIS and
memory systems"*. It is implemented under the `Tiannara.Forecasting.*`
namespace — **not** a second system beside the forecasting machinery.

The public API is a facade over the D1–D5 components:

| Area | Public API |
|------|------------|
| D1 Signal intelligence | `register_signal/1`, `get_signal/1`, `signal_quality/1`, `signal_value/1`, `stats/0`, `health/0` |
| D2 Forecasting | `forecast/1`, `register_forecast/2`, `get_forecast/1`, `score_forecast/2`, `resolve_forecast_outcome/3`, `record_forecast_performance/1`, `forecast_performance_history/2`, `forecast_performance_summary/1`, `temporal_forecast_evaluation/3` |
| D3 Decision intelligence | `decide/1`, `register_decision/1`, `get_decision/1` |
| D4 Counterfactual | `counterfactual_record/1`, `alternative_history/2`, `attribution/3`, `selection/2`, `regression_to_mean/2` |
| D5 Robustness | `tiannara/forecasting/d5/` (9 modules) |
| D6 Institutional memory | **deferred** — `status/0` lists `:memory` under `deferred:` |
| Model update | `assess_forecast_model_update/1` → `ModelUpdateGate` |
| Temporal firewall | `verify_firewall/3` |

> The `efdi.ex` moduledoc still says *"D1 STOPS here and does not forecast,
> calibrate, decide"* while the module plainly does all three. The docstring
> is stale; the code is the authority. Recorded as `TCP-B-043`.

## 3. Inventory

**70 modules** across 49 files in `lib/tiannara/forecasting/`.

| Status | Modules | Meaning |
|--------|---------|---------|
| `implemented` | 17 | Public functions, at least one test reference |
| `partial` | 7 | Public functions, no test reference |
| `disconnected` | 28 | No caller outside the forecasting directory, or nothing to persist |
| `stub` | 18 | Public API returns canned values only |

| Reachability measure | Modules |
|---|---|
| Have at least one test reference | 27 of 70 |
| Have at least one caller outside `lib/tiannara/forecasting/` | 27 of 70 |
| Have **no** caller outside the forecasting directory | **43 of 70** |
| Have some form of persistence | **5 of 70** |

The persistence figure is the headline: **65 of 70 EFDI modules hold no
state across a restart.** EFDI is not a second system — it is a *layer* — but
a layer that keeps nothing cannot support an institutional forecasting
memory, which is D6 and is still deferred.

## 4. What the inventory changed about the plan

The directive's starting claims were verified, with two corrections:

| Claim | Verified? |
|-------|-----------|
| EFDI is the canonical forecasting authority, under `Tiannara.Forecasting` | **Yes.** |
| EFDI and `Tiannara.Forecasting` are the same system, not two | **Yes.** |
| The forecasting namespace holds ~51 modules | **70** (49 files, several defining multiple modules). |
| The Runtime Spine's forecast stage does not call EFDI | **Yes.** It called `ConfidenceEstimator`/`UncertaintyAnalyzer` only. |
| The Research adapter substitutes `1.0 / length(existing)` for information gain | **Yes**, exactly as described. |
| The forecast registry is ETS-backed and does not survive restart | **Yes**, and it also deleted the ETS table on every `init/1`. |
| The World-model adapter returns `:world_snapshot_unavailable` for conflicts | **Yes.** |
| `OutcomeResolution` returns `:resolved_not_certified` / `:requires_independent_review` | **Yes.** |
| `ModelUpdateGate` cannot authorize | **Yes** — it sets `authority: :none`, `authorization: :not_granted`, `deployment: :not_granted`, `production_mutation: :forbidden`, `human_review_required: true`, `acl_required: true`, `oavl_required: true`, `cel_required: true`, `certification_eligible: false`. |

**Correction to the plan.** The directive's Stage 2 asked which integration
mechanism already exists. The inventory of *both* stacks gives the answer:

| Mechanism | Verdict |
|-----------|---------|
| OTP boundary (compile-time dependency) | **Blocked.** 28 module names are defined in both stacks (`Tiannara.Sentinel.*`, `Tiannara.OED.*`, `Tiannara.A10.*`, `Tiannara.CIS.*`, `Tiannara.P9X.*`, `Tiannara.Core.Ontology.Index`, `Tiannara.Meta.CausalTensegrityEngine`, `CivilizationState`). Merging them into one BEAM would redefine modules. That is TCP-002's W1 (stack consolidation), which must precede it. |
| HTTP | The application has a Phoenix `/api/v1` scope; the runtime has `req`. Plausible, but couples the cognitive loop to endpoint availability and a URL, and cannot be exercised here without the full application supervision tree. |
| Message bus (NATS) | The runtime uses NATS extensively (19 phase supervisors). The application has `:gnat` in its dependencies but **one** call site (`lib/tiannara/ucc/trajectory_tensor.ex`). NATS is the one inter-stack dependency both already have. |
| Durable event stream | `Tiannara.Executive.EventStore` is a framed append-only log with replay. It is EFDI's own lineage mechanism. |

**Decision.** The boundary is implemented as a **versioned, transport-agnostic
request/response contract** owned by the application stack, with a NATS
transport on the runtime side. The contract is the deliverable that both
stacks can be held to; the transport is one implementation of it.

## 5. Duplicate and conflicting representations

| Representation | Locations | Finding |
|---|---|---|
| `CognitiveContext` | `TiannaraRuntime.Cognitive.CognitiveContext` and `TiannaraRuntime.Cognitive.Runtime.CognitiveContext` | Two modules, different shapes, no owner (`TCP-B-037`). |
| Signal registry | `Tiannara.Forecasting.SignalRegistry` (EFDI) and `TiannaraRuntime.WorldModel.*` observation registries | Distinct sources; the runtime one feeds the Spine. |
| Forecast registry | `Tiannara.Forecasting.ForecastRegistry` (EFDI, ETS) and `TiannaraRuntime.WorldModel.ModelRegistry` (ETS) | Two registries, two purposes (forecasts vs models). Acceptable, but they must not be confused. |
| Confidence vs probability | `ConfidenceEstimator` (runtime), `Calibration` (EFDI), `SignalValue.information_gain` (EFDI) | Distinct quantities; the Spine previously had no way to obtain a probability at all. |
| Information gain | `SignalValue.compute_information_gain/2` (measured, KL-based) and `ResearchImpl.information_gain_estimate/2` (heuristic fallback) | The fallback presented a heuristic in the `:ok` slot (`TCP-B-041`). |
